text: HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam's construction sector opened a technology exhibition in Hà Nội on November 16, showcasing new products, technologies and solutions for construction, transport and infrastructure.
The exhibition marks the opening of a series of events on science and technology, innovation and digital transformation in the construction industry.

Exhibits cover areas including AI, building information modelling, geographic information systems, smart cities, construction technologies, new materials, green buildings, transport and technical infrastructure.

Featured products and solutions include a tunnel boring machine robot model by FECON; unmanned aerial vehicles, 3D laser scanning technology and digital twins by Portcoast; advanced timber structures by IBST; new construction materials by Viglacera; and models and testing equipment by VTR.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Deputy Minister of Construction Phạm Minh Hà said the sector faces growing demands for technological applications as Việt Nam undertakes major infrastructure projects, including high-speed railways, urban rail systems, expressways, airports and seaports.
These projects require modern construction technologies while meeting standards for quality, delivery schedules, safety and investment efficiency, Hà said.
He added that urban planning, housing development and infrastructure management also needs to use more digital technologies and data to improve management and services for residents and businesses.

Hà said the exhibition provided an opportunity to showcase research and technological applications developed by agencies, organisations and businesses, ranging from materials, equipment and technical solutions for the design, construction and management of projects to information systems, databases and digital solutions.

"What matters is not how many products are on display, but where they can be used, what problems they can solve, and whether they can make work faster, improve quality, reduce costs and enhance management efficiency," Hà said.

He said the exhibition would create more opportunities for agencies, organisations and businesses to exchange information, explore each other's products and strengthen cooperation and transfer technologies, helping bring quality solutions into wider use across the sector.
Alongside the exhibition, the construction sector's science and technology, innovation and digital transformation information portal was launched on the same day.

The portal features 138 notable science and technology products and provides information on strategic technologies, standards, technical regulations, construction norms and digital transformation results.
It is intended to develop a digital knowledge repository for the construction sector, connecting management agencies, scientists, research institutions and businesses. - VNS
